title: Basis for Latest Increase in Electricity Tariffs and Gas Prices
what_it_is: Basis for Latest Increase in Electricity Tariffs and Gas Prices

sections.label: Fuel prices and tariffs rise
sections.summary: Fuel prices rose 46.6% in Q3 2020, and electricity and gas tariffs rose to 22.93 and 17.19 cents/kWh in Q4 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Since dipping to their lowest levels in the past 20 years in April 2020, fuel prices rose by 46.6% in the third quarter of 2020 – the quarter that has just passed – and this is in tandem with the resumption of global economic activity.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: So, the electricity and gas tariffs therefore rose to 22.93 cents/kWh and 17.19 cents/kWh in the fourth quarter this year, as fuel prices rebounded.

sections.label: Q4 2020 electricity tariffs lower
sections.summary: Q4 2020 electricity tariffs remain 11.6% lower than Q1 2020 and 6.7% lower than the January 2018 to September 2020 average.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: For electricity tariffs in particular, it is also worth pointing out that Q4 2020 tariffs still remain at 11.6% lower than Q1 2020 and 6.7% lower than the average electricity tariff between January 2018 and September 2020.

sections.label: Solar capacity target by 2030
sections.summary: Current capacity is 0.4 gigawatt-peak, with a target of at least 2 GWp by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Today, we are at 0.4 gigawatt-peak or GWp.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: We are trying to achieve at least 2 GWp by 2030 – in about 10 years' time.

sections.label: Tariff increase and affected households
sections.summary: Media reported a 9.3% tariff increase for October to December, and the Minister explained about 53% of the population is affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: When the tariff announcement was made, the headline that came up was that there was a 9.3% increase for the month of October to December.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It came across from almost every media outlet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, what the Minister just explained gave a lot of context and details that indeed, only a certain percentage of the population is affected – about 53%.

sections.label: Rebates for HDB flat sizes
sections.summary: One- to two-room flats get six to eight months of rebates, and three- and four-room flats get two to four months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In terms of those rebates, as I have alluded to earlier on, in the 1- to 2-room flats, they get between six and eight months of rebates, and for the 3- and 4-room flats, they get between two and four months.

sections.label: Fixed price electricity plans advice
sections.summary: Most households should consider available plans and move to a fixed price package for more certainty in electricity prices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If it is possible, most households should look at many of these plans that are available and move on to a more fixed price package for more certainty in electricity prices.
